To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
endothelin-3, but not endothelin-1, induces middle cerebral artery occlusions that can be reversed with endothelin-A receptor antagonism.
ET-1 and the ET-3 produced similar volumes of ischemic damage in a rat model of focal cerebral ischemi.

endothelin-3, injected into the brain parenchymal adjacent to the M1 segment of the middle cerebral artery in rats, causes a reproducible, focal ischemia that is amenable to reversal with the endothelin-A receptor antagonist FR139 317.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cerebral ischemia in the rat.
the role of the endothelin system in the pathophysiology of ischemia and the development of new treatments to reduce ischemic damage.
the use of the endothelins as tools to induce cerebral infarction in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ET-3 model is suitable for investigating reperfusion injury in focal cerebral ischemia and that the endothelin-A receptor antagonist FR139337 is a useful tool for studying reperfusion injury.

ET3-induced MCAO is amenable to reversal of occlusion by the ET(A)-receptor antagonist FR139317 and that this model may offer the opportunity to investigate the neuropahology of reperfuson without the procedure-related artifects associated with some reperfusion models.
the model of endothelin-induced middle cerebral artery is a useful model to study the neuropathology and pharmacology of focal cerebral ischemic damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ET-3 induced MCA occlusion with controlled-reperfusion is a reliable and useful model for investigating the pathophysiological mechanisms of ischemia-reperfusion injury.

endothelin-3 induced middle cerebral artery occlusions are amenable to reversal with endothelin-A receptor antagonism, and may be useful for studying the pathophysiology of reperfusion injury in the central nervous system.

endothelin-3 is a more suitable agonist for the induction of middle cerebral artery occlusions in the rat than endothelin-1, and that endothelin-1 is more suitable for inducing transient occlusions than endothelin-3
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ET-3 induced middle cerebral artery occluder is an excellent model for studying the pathophysiology of stroke, especially the effects of reperfusion.
endothelin-1 is an ideal drug to produce focal ischemia in rats, because it is easy to administer, it is highly effective and it does not produce damage to the cerebral endothelium.

we have developed a model of endothelin-induced middle cerebral artery ischemia in the rat that allows for controlled reperfusion, and that this model may be useful to study the pathophysiology of ischemic reperfusion injury.
